head: Chrome update: version 158 fixes a critical sandbox bug
dek: Google's Chrome update of 23 November fixes a critical flaw that could let code run outside the browser's sandbox, on Windows, Mac, Linux and Android. Google's release notes don't report any attacks using it.
details: The fixed builds are 158.0.8127.88 or .89 on Windows and Mac, 158.0.8127.88 on Linux and 158.0.8127.92 on Android; managed computers on the Extended Stable channel get the same fix in 156.0.8078.114. The bug, CVE-2026-134401, is an input check problem in Chrome's Variations component and the only security fix in this release. Android gets it over several days, computers over days or weeks.
where: Chrome on Windows, Mac, Linux and Android, rolling out from 23 November
means: If Chrome hasn't restarted in a while, you may still be on an older build. Updating Chrome on your laptop doesn't update it on your phone.
todo: On a computer, open the menu, then Help, About Google Chrome, let it update and click Relaunch. On Android, open Google Play, tap your profile, then Manage apps & device, and update Chrome. Check every device you use; on a work computer you can't update, tell IT.
